hooks.text: Voyager 1 would need 74,000 years to reach our nearest neighboring star.
Could our fastest spacecraft ever reach the star system next door?
The nearest star is right next door, yet completely unreachable.

title: The 74,000 Year Trip to the Nearest Star
description: Even at 38,000 miles per hour, our fastest spacecraft would take seventy-four millennia to reach Proxima Centauri.

beats.text: Voyager 1 would need 74,000 years to reach our nearest neighboring star.
beats.visual: Artist concept of Voyager 1 in interstellar space

beats.text: We often imagine Proxima Centauri is right next door at just 4.2 light-years away.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of the red dwarf star Proxima Centauri

beats.text: This red dwarf hides a roughly Earth-sized world orbiting within its habitable zone.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the exoplanet Proxima Centauri b and its star
queries: Proxima Centauri b ESO artist concept

beats.text: Proxima Centauri b completes its year in 11.2 days, making it a tempting destination.
beats.visual: Diagram showing the 11.2 day orbit of exoplanet Proxima b

beats.text: There is even a second candidate planet orbiting much further into the cold.
beats.visual: Artist impression of candidate planet Proxima Centauri c

beats.text: Since 1977, Voyager 1 has been racing into the void at 17 kilometers per second.
beats.visual: Launch of the Titan IIIE carrying Voyager 1 from Cape Canaveral

beats.text: But even at that blistering speed, our fastest probe is essentially standing still.
beats.visual: Illustration of Voyager 1 in deep interstellar space

beats.text: The scale of the cosmos makes a human lifetime feel like a heartbeat.
beats.visual: Comparative scale infographic showing the solar system vs nearby stars

beats.text: Bridging the four light-year gap to our neighbors remains a staggering challenge.
beats.visual: Wide field view of the Alpha Centauri and Proxima Centauri system

better_than_last: This script prioritizes a physical scale comparison over historical dates to maximize engagement, as proven in previous scale-based episodes like ep030.
